controls.description: Mechanisms exist to allow individuals to utilize alternative methods of authentication under specific circumstances or situations.

controls.title: Re-Authentication
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to force users and devices to re-authenticate according to organization-defined circumstances that necessitate re-authentication.

controls.title: Account Management
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to proactively govern account management of individual, group, system, service, application, guest and temporary accounts.

controls.title: Automated System Account Management (Directory Services)
controls.description: Automated mechanisms exist to support the management of system accounts (e.g., directory services).

controls.title: Removal of Temporary / Emergency Accounts
controls.description: Automated mechanisms exist to disable or remove temporary and emergency accounts after an organization-defined time period for each type of account.

controls.title: Disable Inactive Accounts
controls.description: Automated mechanisms exist to disable inactive accounts after an organization-defined time period.

controls.title: Restrictions on Shared Groups / Accounts
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to authorize the use of shared/group accounts only under certain organization-defined conditions.

controls.title: System Account Reviews
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to review all system accounts and disable any account that cannot be associated with a business process and owner.

controls.title: Emergency Accounts
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to establish and control "emergency access only" accounts.

controls.title: Privileged Account Management (PAM)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to restrict and control privileged access rights for users and Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).

controls.title: Privileged Account Inventories
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to inventory all privileged accounts and validate that each person with elevated privileges is authorized by the appropriate level of organizational management.

controls.title: Periodic Review of Account Privileges
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to periodically-review the privileges assigned to individuals and service accounts to validate the need for such privileges and reassign or remove unnecessary privileges, as necessary.

controls.title: User Responsibilities for Account Management
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to compel users to follow accepted practices in the use of authentication mechanisms (e.g., passwords, passphrases, physical or logical security tokens, smart cards, certificates, etc.).

controls.title: Credential Sharing
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to prevent the sharing of generic IDs, passwords or other generic authentication methods.

controls.title: Access Enforcement
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to enforce Logical Access Control (LAC) permissions that conform to the principle of "least privilege."

controls.title: Access To Sensitive / Regulated Data
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to limit access to sensitive/regulated data to only those individuals whose job requires such access.

controls.title: Database Access
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to restrict access to databases containing sensitive/regulated data to only necessary Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) or those individuals whose job requires such access.

controls.title: Use of Privileged Utility Programs
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to restrict and tightly control utility programs that are capable of overriding system and application controls.

controls.title: Revocation of Access Authorizations
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to revoke logical and physical access authorizations.

controls.title: Least Privilege
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize the concept of least privilege, allowing only authorized access to processes necessary to accomplish assigned tasks in accordance with organizational business functions.

controls.title: Management Approval For Privileged Accounts
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to restrict the assignment of privileged accounts to management-approved personnel and/or roles.

controls.title: Auditing Use of Privileged Functions
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to audit the execution of privileged functions.

controls.title: Account Lockout
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to enforce a limit for consecutive invalid login attempts by a user during an organization-defined time period and automatically locks the account when the maximum number of unsuccessful attempts is exceeded.

controls.title: Session Lock
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to initiate a session lock after an organization-defined time period of inactivity, or upon receiving a request from a user and retain the session lock until the user reestablishes access using established identification and authentication methods.

controls.title: Session Termination
controls.description: Automated mechanisms exist to log out users, both locally on the network and for remote sessions, at the end of the session or after an organization-defined period of inactivity.

controls.title: Identity Proofing (Identity Verification)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to verify the identity of a user before issuing authenticators or modifying access permissions.

controls.title: Management Approval For New or Changed Accounts
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure management approvals are required for new accounts or changes in permissions to existing accounts.

controls.title: Identity Evidence
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to require evidence of individual identification to be presented to the registration authority.

controls.title: Identity Evidence Validation & Verification
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to require that the presented identity evidence be validated and verified through organizational-defined methods of validation and verification.

controls.title: Information Assurance (IA) Operations
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of security, compliance and resilience assessment and authorization controls.

controls.title: Assessment Boundaries
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to establish the scope of assessments by defining the assessment boundary, according to people, processes and technology that directly or indirectly impact the confidentiality, integrity, availability and safety of the Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) under review.

controls.title: Assessments
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to formally assess the security, compliance and resilience controls in Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) through Information Assurance Program (IAP) activities to determine the extent to which the controls are implemented correctly, operating as intended and producing the desired outcome with respect to meeting expected requirements.

controls.title: Assessor Independence
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure assessors or assessment teams have the appropriate independence to conduct security, compliance and/or resilience control assessments.

controls.title: Specialized Assessments
Security Assessment Report (SAR)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to produce a Security Assessment Report (SAR) at the conclusion of a security assessment to certify the results of the assessment and assist with any remediation actions.

controls.title: Applied Security, Compliance and Resilience Controls Documentation
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to generate authoritative documentation (e.g., System Security Plan (SSP)) that:
(1) Identifies key architectural and implementation information on in-scope Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS);
(2) Reflects the current state of applied security, compliance and resilience controls on applicable People, Processes, Technologies, Data and/or Facilities (PPTDF) that are contained within the system boundary; and
(3) Provides a historical record of applied security controls, including changes.

controls.title: Plan / Coordinate with Other Organizational Entities
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to plan and coordinate Information Assurance Program (IAP) activities with affected stakeholders before conducting such activities in order to reduce the potential impact on operations.

controls.title: Adequate Security for Sensitive / Regulated Data In Support of Contracts
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to protect sensitive/regulated data that is collected, developed, received, transmitted, used or stored in support of the performance of a contract.

controls.title: Threat Analysis & Flaw Remediation During Development
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to require system developers and integrators to create and execute a Security Testing and Evaluation (ST&E) plan, or similar process, to identify and remediate flaws during development.

controls.title: Capabilities Deficiency Tracking
Technical Verification
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to perform Information Assurance Program (IAP) activities to evaluate the design, implementation and effectiveness of technical security, compliance and resilience controls.

controls.title: Security Authorization
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) are officially authorized prior to "go live" in a production environment.

controls.title: Incident Response Operations
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement and govern processes and documentation to facilitate an organization-wide response capability for cybersecurity and data protection-related incidents.

controls.title: Incident Handling
Incident Classification & Prioritization
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to identify classes of incidents and actions to take to ensure the continuation of organizational missions and business functions.

controls.title: Correlation with External Organizations
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to coordinate with approved third-parties to achieve a cross-organization perspective on incident awareness and more effective incident responses.

controls.title: Indicators of Compromise (IOC)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to define specific Indicators of Compromise (IOC) to identify the signs of potential cybersecurity events.

controls.title: Incident Response Plan (IRP)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to maintain and make available a current and viable Incident Response Plan (IRP) to all stakeholders.

controls.title: Data Breach
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to address data breaches, or other incidents involving the unauthorized disclosure of sensitive or regulated data, according to applicable laws, regulations and contractual obligations.

controls.title: IRP Update
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to regularly review and modify incident response practices to incorporate lessons learned, business process changes and industry developments, as necessary.

controls.title: Incident Response Training
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to train personnel in their incident response roles and responsibilities.

controls.title: Incident Response Testing
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to formally test incident response capabilities through realistic exercises to determine the operational effectiveness of those capabilities.

controls.title: Coordination with Related Plans
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to coordinate incident response testing with organizational elements responsible for related plans.

controls.title: Integrated Security Incident Response Team (ISIRT)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to establish an integrated team of cybersecurity, IT and business function representatives that are capable of addressing cybersecurity and data protection incident response operations.

controls.title: Chain of Custody & Forensics
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to perform digital forensics and maintain the integrity of the chain of custody, in accordance with applicable laws, regulations and industry-recognized secure practices.

controls.title: Situational Awareness For Incidents
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to document, monitor and report the status of cybersecurity and data protection incidents to internal stakeholders all the way through the resolution of the incident.

controls.title: Incident Stakeholder Reporting
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to timely-report incidents to applicable:
(1) Internal stakeholders; 
(2) Affected clients & third-parties; and
(3) Regulatory authorities.

controls.title: Cyber Incident Reporting for Sensitive / Regulated Data
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to report sensitive/regulated data incidents in a timely manner.

controls.title: Vulnerabilities Related To Incidents
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to report system vulnerabilities associated with reported cybersecurity and data protection incidents to organization-defined personnel or roles.

controls.title: Supply Chain Coordination
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to provide cybersecurity and data protection incident information to the provider of the Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) and other organizations involved in the supply chain for TAAS related to the incident.

controls.title: Coordination With External Providers
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to establish a direct, cooperative relationship between the organization's incident response capability and external service providers.

controls.title: Sensitive / Regulated Data Spill Response
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to respond to sensitive/regulated data spills.

controls.title: Post-Sensitive / Regulated Data Spill Operations
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure that organizational personnel impacted by sensitive/regulated data spills can continue to carry out assigned tasks while contaminated Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) are undergoing corrective actions.

controls.title: Root Cause Analysis (RCA) & Lessons Learned
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to incorporate lessons learned from analyzing and resolving cybersecurity and data protection incidents to reduce the likelihood or impact of future incidents.

controls.title: Regulatory & Law Enforcement Contacts
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to maintain incident response contacts with applicable regulatory and law enforcement agencies.

controls.title: Public Relations & Reputation Repair
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to proactively manage public relations associated with incidents and employ appropriate measures to prevent further reputational damage and develop plans to repair any damage to the organization's reputation.

controls.title: Centralized Management Of Mobile Devices
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement and govern Mobile Device Management (MDM) controls.

controls.title: Access Control For Mobile Devices
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to enforce access control requirements for the connection of mobile devices to organizational Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).

controls.title: Full Device & Container-Based Encryption
controls.description: Cryptographic mechanisms exist to protect the confidentiality and integrity of information on mobile devices through full-device or container encryption.

controls.title: Remote Purging
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to remotely purge selected information from mobile devices.

controls.title: Maintenance Operations
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to develop, disseminate, review & update procedures to facilitate the implementation of maintenance controls across the enterprise.

controls.title: Controlled Maintenance
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to conduct controlled maintenance activities throughout the lifecycle of the Technology Asset, Application and/or Service (TAAS).

controls.title: Timely Maintenance
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to obtain maintenance support and/or spare parts for Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) within a defined Recovery Time Objective (RTO).

controls.title: Preventative Maintenance
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to perform preventive maintenance on critical Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).

controls.title: Prevent Unauthorized Removal
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to prevent or control the removal of equipment undergoing maintenance that contains organizational information.

controls.title: Remote Maintenance
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to authorize, monitor and control remote, non-local maintenance and diagnostic activities.

controls.title: Auditing Remote Maintenance
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to audit remote, non-local maintenance and diagnostic sessions, as well as review the maintenance action performed during remote maintenance sessions.

controls.title: Remote Maintenance Cryptographic Protection
controls.description: Cryptographic mechanisms exist to protect the integrity and confidentiality of remote, non-local maintenance and diagnostic communications.

controls.title: Remote Maintenance Disconnect Verification
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to provide remote disconnect verification to ensure remote, non-local maintenance and diagnostic sessions are properly terminated.

controls.title: Continuous Monitoring
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of enterprise-wide monitoring controls.

controls.title: Intrusion Detection & Prevention Systems (IDS & IPS)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement Intrusion Detection / Prevention Systems (IDS / IPS) technologies on critical systems, key network segments and network choke points.

controls.title: Deactivated Account Activity
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to monitor deactivated accounts for attempted usage.

controls.title: Automated Response to Suspicious Events
controls.description: Automated mechanisms exist to implement pre-determined corrective actions in response to detected events that have security incident implications.

controls.title: Automated Alerts
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to automatically alert incident response personnel to inappropriate or anomalous activities that have potential security incident implications.

controls.title: Privileged User Oversight
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement enhanced activity monitoring for privileged users.

controls.title: Analyze and Prioritize Monitoring Requirements
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to assess the organization's needs for monitoring and prioritize the monitoring of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS), based on TAAS criticality and the sensitivity of the data it stores, transmits and processes.

controls.title: Automated Tools for Real-Time Analysis
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize a Security Incident Event Manager (SIEM), or similar automated tool, to support near real-time analysis and incident escalation.

controls.title: Inbound & Outbound Communications Traffic
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to continuously monitor inbound and outbound communications traffic for unusual or unauthorized activities or conditions.

controls.title: System Generated Alerts
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to generate, monitor, correlate and respond to alerts from physical, cybersecurity, data protection and supply chain activities to achieve integrated situational awareness.

controls.title: Wireless Network Monitoring
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to monitor wireless network segments for:
(1) Rogue wireless devices; and
(2) Anomalous and/or hostile activities.

controls.title: Host-Based Devices
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize Host-based Intrusion Detection / Prevention Systems (HIDS / HIPS) to actively alert on or block unwanted activities and send logs to a Security Incident Event Manager (SIEM), or similar automated tool, to maintain situational awareness.

controls.title: File Integrity Monitoring (FIM)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize a File Integrity Monitor (FIM), or similar change-detection technology, on critical Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to generate alerts for unauthorized modifications.

controls.title: Security Event Monitoring
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to review event logs on an ongoing basis and escalate incidents in accordance with established timelines and procedures.

controls.title: Centralized Collection of Security Event Logs
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize a Security Incident Event Manager (SIEM), or similar automated tool, to support the centralized collection of security-related event logs.

controls.title: Correlate Monitoring Information
controls.description: Automated mechanisms exist to correlate both technical and non-technical information from across the enterprise by a Security Incident Event Manager (SIEM) or similar automated tool, to enhance organization-wide situational awareness.

controls.title: Central Review & Analysis
controls.description: Automated mechanisms exist to centrally collect, review and analyze audit records from multiple sources.

controls.title: System-Wide / Time-Correlated Audit Trail
controls.description: Automated mechanisms exist to compile audit records into an organization-wide audit trail that is time-correlated.

controls.title: Content of Event Logs
Audit Trails
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to link system access to individual users or service accounts.

controls.title: Privileged Functions Logging
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to log and review the actions of users and/or services with elevated privileges.

controls.title: Database Logging
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure databases produce audit records that contain sufficient information to monitor database activities.

controls.title: Response To Event Log Processing Failures
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to alert appropriate personnel in the event of a log processing failure and take actions to remedy the disruption.

controls.title: Monitoring Reporting
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to provide an event log report generation capability to aid in detecting and assessing anomalous activities.

controls.title: Time Stamps
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to configure Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to use an authoritative time source to generate time stamps for event logs.

controls.title: Synchronization With Authoritative Time Source
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to synchronize internal system clocks with an authoritative time source.

controls.title: Protection of Event Logs
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to protect event logs and audit tools from unauthorized access, modification and deletion.

controls.title: Event Log Backup on Separate Physical Systems / Components
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to back up event logs onto a physically different system or system component than the Security Incident Event Manager (SIEM) or similar automated tool.

controls.title: Access by Subset of Privileged Users
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to restrict access to the management of event logs to privileged users with a specific business need.

controls.title: Event Log Retention
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to retain event logs for a time period consistent with records retention requirements to provide support for after-the-fact investigations of security incidents and to meet statutory, regulatory and contractual retention requirements.

controls.title: Monitoring For Information Disclosure
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to monitor for evidence of unauthorized exfiltration or disclosure of non-public information.

controls.title: Analyze Traffic for Covert Exfiltration
controls.description: Automated mechanisms exist to analyze network traffic to detect covert data exfiltration.

controls.title: Monitoring for Indicators of Compromise (IOC)
controls.description: Automated mechanisms exist to identify and alert on Indicators of Compromise (IoC).

controls.title: Covert Channel Analysis
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to conduct covert channel analysis to identify aspects of communications that are potential avenues for covert channels.

controls.title: Anomalous Behavior
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize User & Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) and/or User Activity Monitoring (UAM) solutions to detect and respond to anomalous behavior that could indicate account compromise or other malicious activities.

controls.title: Insider Threats
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to monitor internal personnel activity for potential security incidents.

controls.title: Third-Party Threats
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to monitor third-party personnel activity for potential security incidents.

controls.title: Unauthorized Activities
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to monitor for unauthorized activities, accounts, connections, devices and software.

controls.title: Account Creation and Modification Logging
controls.description: Automated mechanisms exist to generate event logs for permissions changes to privileged accounts and/or groups.

controls.title: Network Security Controls (NSC)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to develop, govern & update procedures to facilitate the implementation of Network Security Controls (NSC).

controls.title: Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to treat all users and devices as potential threats and prevent access to data and resources until the users can be properly authenticated and their access authorized.

controls.title: Layered Network Defenses
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement security functions as a layered structure that minimizes interactions between layers of the design and avoids any dependence by lower layers on the functionality or correctness of higher layers.

controls.title: Guest Networks
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement and manage a secure guest network.

controls.title: Boundary Protection
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to monitor and control communications at the external network boundary and at key internal boundaries within the network.

controls.title: Limit Network Connections
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to limit the number of concurrent external network connections to its Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).

controls.title: Prevent Discovery of Internal Information
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to prevent the public disclosure of internal network information.

controls.title: Prevent Unauthorized Exfiltration
controls.description: Automated mechanisms exist to prevent the unauthorized exfiltration of sensitive/regulated data across managed interfaces.

controls.title: Isolation of System Components
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to employ boundary protections to isolate Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) that support critical missions and/or business functions.

controls.title: Separate Subnet for Connecting to Different Security Domains
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement separate network addresses (e.g., different subnets) to connect to systems in different security domains.

controls.title: Data Flow Enforcement – Access Control Lists (ACLs)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement and govern Access Control Lists (ACLs) to provide data flow enforcement that explicitly restrict network traffic to only what is authorized.

controls.title: Deny Traffic by Default & Allow Traffic by Exception
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to configure firewall and router configurations to deny network traffic by default and allow network traffic by exception (e.g., deny all, permit by exception).

controls.title: Human Reviews
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to enforce the use of human reviews for Access Control Lists (ACLs) and similar rulesets on a routine basis.

controls.title: Policy Decision Point (PDP)
controls.description: Automated mechanisms exist to evaluate access requests against established criteria to dynamically and uniformly enforce access rights and permissions.

controls.title: External System Connections
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to prohibit the direct connection of a sensitive system to an external network without the use of an organization-defined boundary protection device.

controls.title: Network Segmentation (macrosegementation)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure network architecture utilizes network segmentation to isolate Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to protect from other network resources.

controls.title: Security Management Subnets
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement security management subnets to isolate security tools and support components from other internal system components by implementing separate subnetworks with managed interfaces to other components of the system.

controls.title: Network Connection Termination
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to terminate network connections at the end of a session or after an organization-defined time period of inactivity.

controls.title: Network Intrusion Detection / Prevention Systems (NIDS / NIPS)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to employ Network Intrusion Detection / Prevention Systems (NIDS/NIPS) to detect and/or prevent intrusions into the network.

controls.title: DMZ Networks
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to monitor De-Militarized Zone (DMZ) network segments to separate untrusted networks from trusted networks.

controls.title: Wireless Intrusion Detection / Prevention Systems (WIDS / WIPS) Deployment
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize Wireless Intrusion Detection / Protection Systems (WIDS / WIPS) on wireless network segments.

controls.title: Session Integrity
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to protect the authenticity and integrity of communications sessions.

controls.title: Safeguarding Data Over Open Networks
controls.description: Cryptographic mechanisms exist to implement strong cryptography and security protocols to safeguard sensitive/regulated data during transmission over open, public networks.

controls.title: Wireless Link Protection
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to protect external and internal wireless links from signal parameter attacks through monitoring for unauthorized wireless connections, including scanning for unauthorized wireless access points and taking appropriate action, if an unauthorized connection is discovered.

controls.title: End-User Messaging Technologies
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to prohibit the transmission of unprotected sensitive/regulated data by end-user messaging technologies.

controls.title: Electronic Messaging
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to protect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of electronic messaging communications.

controls.title: Remote Access
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to define, control and review organization-approved, secure remote access methods.

controls.title: Managed Access Control Points
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to route all remote accesses through managed network access control points (e.g., VPN concentrator).

controls.title: Work From Anywhere (WFA) - Telecommuting Security
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to define secure telecommuting practices and govern remote access to Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) for remote workers.

controls.title: Third-Party Remote Access Governance
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to proactively control and monitor third-party accounts used to access, support, or maintain system components via remote access.

controls.title: Wireless Networking
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to control authorized wireless usage and monitor for unauthorized wireless access.

controls.title: Authentication & Encryption
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to secure Wi-Fi (e.g., IEEE 802.11) and prevent unauthorized access by:
(1) Authenticating devices trying to connect; and 
(2) Encrypting transmitted data.

controls.title: Rogue Wireless Detection
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to test for the presence of Wireless Access Points (WAPs) and identify all authorized and unauthorized WAPs within the facility(ies).

controls.title: Data Loss Prevention (DLP)
controls.description: Automated mechanisms exist to implement Data Loss Prevention (DLP) to protect sensitive information as it is stored, transmitted and processed.

controls.title: DNS & Content Filtering
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to force Internet-bound network traffic through a proxy device (e.g., Policy Enforcement Point (PEP)) for URL content filtering and DNS filtering to limit a user's ability to connect to dangerous or prohibited Internet sites.

controls.title: Operations Security
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of operational security controls.

controls.title: Standardized Operating Procedures (SOP)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to identify and document Standardized Operating Procedures (SOP), or similar documentation, to enable the proper execution of day-to-day / assigned tasks.

controls.title: Security Concept Of Operations (CONOPS)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to develop a security Concept of Operations (CONOPS), or a similarly-defined plan for achieving cybersecurity objectives, that documents management, operational and technical measures implemented to apply defense-in-depth techniques that is communicated to all appropriate stakeholders.

controls.title:
Service Delivery
(Business Process Support)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to define supporting business processes and implement appropriate governance and service management to ensure appropriate planning, delivery and support of the organization's technology capabilities supporting business functions, workforce, and/or customers based on industry-recognized standards to achieve the specific goals of the process area.

controls.title: Secure Practices Guidelines
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to provide guidelines and recommendations for the secure use of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to assist in the configuration, installation and use of the product and/or service.

controls.title: Physical & Environmental Protections
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the operation of physical and environmental protection controls.

controls.title: Physical Access Authorizations
controls.description: Physical access control mechanisms exist to maintain a current list of personnel with authorized access to organizational facilities (except for those areas within the facility officially designated as publicly accessible).

controls.title: Role-Based Physical Access
controls.description: Physical access control mechanisms exist to authorize physical access to facilities based on the position or role of the individual.

controls.title: Physical Access Control
controls.description: Physical access control mechanisms exist to enforce physical access authorizations for all physical access points (including designated entry/exit points) to facilities (excluding those areas within the facility officially designated as publicly accessible).

controls.title: Controlled Ingress & Egress Points
controls.description: Physical access control mechanisms exist to limit and monitor physical access through controlled ingress and egress points.

controls.title: Lockable Physical Casings
controls.description: Physical access control mechanisms exist to protect system components from unauthorized physical access (e.g., lockable physical casings).

controls.title: Physical Access Logs
controls.description: Physical access control mechanisms generate a log entry for each access attempt through controlled ingress and egress points.

controls.title: Access To Critical Systems
controls.description: Physical access control mechanisms exist to enforce physical access to critical systems or sensitive/regulated data, in addition to the physical access controls for the facility.

controls.title: Physical Security of Offices, Rooms & Facilities
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to identify systems, equipment and respective operating environments that require limited physical access so that appropriate physical access controls are designed and implemented for offices, rooms and facilities.

controls.title: Working in Secure Areas
controls.description: Physical security mechanisms exist to allow only authorized personnel access to secure areas.

controls.title: Monitoring Physical Access
controls.description: Physical access control mechanisms exist to monitor for, detect and respond to physical security incidents.

controls.title: Intrusion Alarms / Surveillance Equipment
controls.description: Physical access control mechanisms exist to monitor physical intrusion alarms and surveillance equipment.

controls.title: Monitoring Physical Access To Critical Systems
controls.description: Facility security mechanisms exist to monitor physical access to critical systems or sensitive/regulated data, in addition to the physical access monitoring of the facility.

controls.title: Visitor Control
controls.description: Physical access control mechanisms exist to identify, authorize and monitor visitors before allowing access to the facility (other than areas designated as publicly accessible).

controls.title: Distinguish Visitors from On-Site Personnel
controls.description: Physical access control mechanisms exist to easily distinguish between onsite personnel and visitors, especially in areas where sensitive/regulated data is accessible.

controls.title: Identification Requirement
controls.description: Physical access control mechanisms exist to requires at least one(1) form of government-issued or organization-issued photo identification to authenticate individuals before they can gain access to the facility.

controls.title: Restrict Unescorted Access
controls.description: Physical access control mechanisms exist to restrict unescorted access to facilities to personnel with required security clearances, formal access authorizations and validate the need for access.

controls.title: Automated Records Management & Review
controls.description: Automated mechanisms exist to facilitate the maintenance and review of visitor access records.

controls.title: Minimize Visitor Personal Data (PD)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to minimize the collection of Personal Data (PD) contained in visitor access records.

controls.title: Visitor Access Revocation
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure visitor badges, or other issued identification, are surrendered before visitors leave the facility or are deactivated at a pre-determined time/date of expiration.

controls.title: Supporting Utilities
controls.description: Facility security mechanisms exist to protect power equipment and power cabling for the system from damage and destruction.

controls.title: Automatic Voltage Controls
controls.description: Facility security mechanisms exist to utilize automatic voltage controls for critical system components.

controls.title: Emergency Shutoff
controls.description:
Facility security mechanisms exist to shut off power in emergency situations by:
(1) Placing emergency shutoff switches or devices in close proximity to systems or system components to facilitate safe and easy access for personnel; and
(2) Protecting emergency power shutoff capability from unauthorized activation.

controls.title: Emergency Power
controls.description: Facility security mechanisms exist to supply alternate power, capable of maintaining minimally-required operational capability, in the event of an extended loss of the primary power source.

controls.title: Emergency Lighting
controls.description: Facility security mechanisms exist to utilize and maintain automatic emergency lighting that activates in the event of a power outage or disruption and that covers emergency exits and evacuation routes within the facility.

controls.title: Water Damage Protection
controls.description: Facility security mechanisms exist to protect systems from damage resulting from water leakage by providing master shutoff valves that are accessible, working properly and known to key personnel.

controls.title: Fire Protection
controls.description: Facility security mechanisms exist to utilize and maintain fire suppression and detection devices/systems for the system that are supported by an independent energy source.

controls.title: Fire Detection Devices
controls.description: Facility security mechanisms exist to utilize and maintain fire detection devices/systems that activate automatically and notify organizational personnel and emergency responders in the event of a fire.

controls.title: Fire Suppression Devices
controls.description: Facility security mechanisms exist to utilize fire suppression devices/systems that provide automatic notification of any activation to organizational personnel and emergency responders.

controls.title: Temperature & Humidity Controls
controls.description: Facility security mechanisms exist to maintain and monitor temperature and humidity levels within the facility.

controls.title: Monitoring with Alarms / Notifications
controls.description: Facility security mechanisms exist to trigger an alarm or notification of temperature and humidity changes that be potentially harmful to personnel or equipment.

controls.title: Delivery & Removal
controls.description: Physical security mechanisms exist to isolate information processing facilities from points such as delivery and loading areas and other points to avoid unauthorized access.

controls.title: Alternate Work Site
controls.description: Physical security mechanisms exist to utilize appropriate management, operational and technical controls at alternate work sites.

controls.title: Equipment Siting & Protection
controls.description: Physical security mechanisms exist to locate system components within the facility to minimize potential damage from physical and environmental hazards and to minimize the opportunity for unauthorized access.

controls.title: Transmission Medium Security
controls.description: Physical security mechanisms exist to protect power and telecommunications cabling carrying data or supporting information services from interception, interference or damage.

controls.title: Access Control for Output Devices
controls.description: Physical security mechanisms exist to restrict access to printers and other system output devices to prevent unauthorized individuals from obtaining the output.

controls.title: Information Leakage Due To Electromagnetic Signals Emanations
controls.description: Facility security mechanisms exist to protect the system from information leakage due to electromagnetic signals emanations.

controls.title: Electromagnetic Pulse (EMP) Protection
controls.description: Physical security mechanisms exist to employ safeguards against Electromagnetic Pulse (EMP) damage for systems and system components.

controls.title: Data Privacy Program
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation and operation of data protection controls throughout the data lifecycle to ensure all forms of Personal Data (PD) are processed lawfully, fairly and transparently.

controls.title: Privacy Act Statements
Dissemination of Data Privacy Program Information
Data Protection Officer (DPO)
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to appoint a Data Protection Officer (DPO):
(1) Based on professional qualifications; and
(2) To be involved in all issues related to how Personal Data (PD) is collected, received, processed, stored, transmitted, shared, updated and/or disposed.

controls.title: Binding Corporate Rules (BCR)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement and manage Binding Corporate Rules (BCR) (e.g., data sharing agreement) to legally-bind all parties engaged in a joint economic activity that contractually states enforceable rights on data subjects with regard to the processing of their personal data.

controls.title: Security of Personal Data (PD)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure Personal Data (PD) is protected by logical and physical security safeguards that are sufficient and appropriately scoped to protect the confidentiality and integrity of the PD.

controls.title: Limiting Personal Data (PD) Disclosures
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to limit the disclosure of Personal Data (PD) to authorized parties for the sole purpose for which the PD was obtained.

controls.title: Data Privacy Notice
Purpose Specification
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure data privacy notices identify the purpose(s) for which Personal Data (PD) is collected, received, processed, stored, transmitted and/or shared.

controls.title: Choice & Consent
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to enable data subjects to authorize the collection, receiving, processing, storage, transmission, sharing, updating and/or disposal of their Personal Data (PD), where prior to collection the data subject is provided with:
(1) Plain language to illustrate the potential data privacy risks of the authorization; 
(2) A means for users to decline the authorization; and
(3) All necessary choice and consent-related criteria required by applicable statutory, regulatory and contractual obligations.

controls.title: Tailored Consent
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to allow data subjects to modify permission to collect, receive, process, store, transmit, share, update and/or dispose selected attributes of their Personal Data (PD).

controls.title: Communicating Processing Changes
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to notify data subjects of processing changes affecting their Personal Data (PD), including:
(1) Erasure of PD;
(2) Remediation of incorrect PD; and/or
(3) Processing restrictions affecting their PD.

controls.title: Just-In-Time Notice & Updated Consent
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to present data subjects with a new or updated consent request to collect, receive, process, store, transmit, share, update and/or dispose Personal Data (PD) in conjunction with the data action, when:
(1) The original circumstances under which an individual gave consent have changed; or
(2) A significant amount of time has passed since an individual gave consent.

controls.title: Revoke Consent
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to allow data subjects to revoke consent to collect, receive, process, store, transmit, share and/or update their Personal Data (PD).

controls.title: Authorized Agent
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to allow data subjects to authorize another person or entity (e.g., authorized agent, proxy, etc.), acting on the data subject's behalf, to make Personal Data (PD) processing decisions.

controls.title: Continued Use of Personal Data (PD)
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to govern the continued use of Personal Data (PD) as it is collected, received, processed, stored, transmitted, shared and/or updated until:
(1) Disposal of PD occurs when there is no longer a legitimate business purpose;
(2) Disposal of PD occurs when the data retention timeline for the use case is met; and/or
(3) Continued use of PD is prohibited upon withdrawal of data subject consent.

controls.title: Restrict Collection To Identified Purpose
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to minimize the collection of Personal Data (PD) to only what is adequate, relevant and limited to the purposes identified in the data privacy notice, including protections against collecting PD from minors without appropriate parental or legal guardian consent.

controls.title: Authority To Collect, Process, Store & Share Personal Data (PD)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to determine and document the legal authority that permits the organization to collect, receive, process, store, transmit, share, update and/or dispose Personal Data (PD), either generally or in support of a specific business process.

controls.title: Primary Sources
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure information is directly collected from the data subject, whenever possible.

controls.title: Personal Data (PD) Retention & Disposal
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to: 
(1) Retain Personal Data (PD), including metadata, for an organization-defined time period to fulfill the purpose(s) identified in the notice or as required by law;
(2) Dispose of, destroys, erases, and/or anonymizes the PD, regardless of the method of storage; and
(3) Use organization-defined techniques or methods to ensure secure deletion or destruction of PD (including originals, copies and archived records).

controls.title: Internal Use of Personal Data (PD) For Testing, Training and Research
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to address the use of Personal Data (PD) for internal testing, training and research that:
(1) Takes measures to limit or minimize the amount of PD used for internal testing, training and research purposes; and
(2) Authorizes the use of PD when such information is required for internal testing, training and research.

controls.title: Personal Data (PD) Accuracy & Integrity
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to ensure the accuracy and relevance of Personal Data (PD) throughout the information lifecycle by:
(1) Keeping PD up-to-date; and 
(2) Remediating identified inaccuracies, as necessary.

controls.title: Data Masking
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to mask sensitive/regulated data through data anonymization, pseudonymization, redaction or de-identification.

controls.title: Usage Restrictions of Personal Data (PD)
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to restrict collecting, receiving, processing, storing, transmitting, sharing and/or updating Personal Data (PD) to:
(1) The purpose(s) originally collected, consistent with the data privacy notice(s);
(2) What is authorized by the data subject, or authorized agent; and
(3) What is consistent with applicable laws, regulations and contractual obligations.

controls.title: Inventory of Personal Data (PD)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to establish and maintain a current inventory of all Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) that collect, receive, process, store, transmit, share, update and/or dispose Personal Data (PD).

controls.title: Personal Data (PD) Categories
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to define and implement data handling and protection requirements for specific categories of sensitive Personal Data (PD).

controls.title: Personal Data (PD) Formats
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to retain Personal Data (PD) in a format permitting data subject identification for no longer than is necessary for legitimate business purposes.

controls.title: Data Subject Empowerment
Correcting Inaccurate Personal Data (PD)
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to maintain a process for:
(1) Data subjects to have inaccurate Personal Data (PD) maintained by the organization corrected or amended; and
(2) Disseminating corrections or amendments of PD to other authorized users of the PD.

controls.title: Notice of Correction or Processing Change
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to notify affected data subjects if their Personal Data (PD) has been corrected, amended or deleted.

controls.title: Appeal Adverse Decision
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to maintain a process for data subjects to appeal an adverse decision.

controls.title: User Feedback Management
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to maintain a process to efficiently and effectively respond to requests, complaints, concerns or questions from authenticated data subjects about Personal Data (PD) the organization collects, receives, processes, stores, transmits, shares, updates and/or disposes.

controls.title: Right to Erasure
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to maintain a process to erase a data subject's Personal Data (PD), in accordance with applicable laws, regulations and contractual obligations pertaining to the retention of their PD.

controls.title: Data Portability
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to format exports of Personal Data (PD) in a structured, machine-readable format that allows data subjects to transfer their PD to another controller without hindrance.

controls.title: Personal Data (PD) Exports
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to export a data subject's available Personal Data (PD) in a readily usable format, upon an authenticated request.

controls.title: Information Sharing With Third Parties
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to disclose Personal Data (PD) to third-parties only for the purposes identified in the data privacy notice and with the implicit or explicit consent of the data subject.

controls.title: Data Privacy Requirements for Contractors & Service Providers
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to include data privacy requirements in contracts and other acquisition-related documents that establish data privacy roles and responsibilities for contractors and service providers.

controls.title: Reject Unauthenticated or Untrustworthy Disclosure Requests
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to reject unauthenticated, or untrustworthy, disclosure requests.

controls.title: Personal Data (PD) Control Testing, Training & Monitoring
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to conduct testing, training and monitoring activities for Personal Data (PD) controls.

controls.title: Data Quality Management
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to manage the quality, utility, objectivity, integrity and impact determination and de-identification of sensitive/regulated data across the information lifecycle.

controls.title: Updating Personal Data (PD) Process
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to identify and record:
(1) The process(es) used to update Personal Data (PD); and
(2) The frequency that such updates occur.

controls.title: Documenting Data Processing Activities
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to document Personal Data (PD) processing activities that covers collection, receiving, processing, storage, transmission, sharing, updating and/or disposal actions with sufficient detail to demonstrate conformity with applicable statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements.

controls.title: Accounting of Disclosures
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to provide data subjects with an accounting of disclosures of their Personal Data (PD) controlled by:
(1) The organization; and/or
(2) Relevant third-parties that their PD was shared with.

controls.title: Data Subject Communications
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to craft disclosures and communications to data subjects in a manner that is concise, unambiguous and understandable by a reasonable person.

controls.title: Data Controller Communications
Security, Compliance & Resilience Protection Portfolio Management
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of resource planning controls that provide a portfolio management approach to achieve security, compliance and resilience objectives.

controls.title: Strategic Plan & Objectives
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to establish a:
(1) Strategic security, compliance and resilience-specific business plan; and 
(2) Set of objectives to achieve that plan.

controls.title: Targeted Capability Maturity Levels
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to define and identify targeted capability maturity levels.

controls.title: Security, Compliance & Resilience Resource Management
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to address all capital planning and investment requests, including the resources needed to implement the Security, Compliance & Resilience Program (SCRP) and document all exceptions to this requirement.

controls.title: Allocation of Resources
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to identify and allocate resources for management, operational, technical and data protection requirements within business process planning for projects / initiatives.

controls.title: Security, Compliance & Resilience In Project Management
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to assess security, compliance and resilience controls in system project development to determine the extent to which the controls are implemented correctly, operating as intended and producing the desired outcome with respect to meeting the requirements.

controls.title: Security, Compliance & Resilience Requirements Definition
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to identify critical system components and functions by performing a criticality analysis for critical Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) at pre-defined decision points in the Secure Development Life Cycle (SDLC).

controls.title: Business Process Definition
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to define business processes with consideration for security, compliance and resilience that determines: 
(1) The resulting risk to organizational operations, assets, individuals and other organizations; and
(2) Information protection needs arising from the defined business processes and revises the processes as necessary, until an achievable set of protection needs is obtained.

controls.title: Secure Development Life Cycle (SDLC) Management
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure changes to Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) within the Secure Development Life Cycle (SDLC) are controlled through formal change control procedures.

controls.title: Risk Management Program
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of strategic, operational and tactical risk management controls.

controls.title: Risk Framing
Risk Management Resourcing
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to reduce the magnitude or likelihood of potential impacts by resourcing the capability required to manage technology-related risks.

controls.title: Risk Tolerance
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to define organizational risk tolerance, the specified range of acceptable results.

controls.title: Risk Threshold
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to define organizational risk threshold, the level of risk exposure above which risks are addressed and below which risks may be accepted.

controls.title: Risk Appetite
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to define organizational risk appetite, the degree of uncertainty the organization is willing to accept in anticipation of a reward.

controls.title: Risk-Based Security Categorization
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to categorize Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) in accordance with applicable laws, regulations and contractual obligations that:
(1) Document the security categorization results (including supporting rationale) in the security plan for systems; and
(2) Ensure the security categorization decision is reviewed and approved by the asset owner.

controls.title: Impact-Level Prioritization
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to prioritize the impact level for Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to prevent potential disruptions.

controls.title: Risk Identification
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to identify and document risks, both internal and external.

controls.title: Risk Catalog
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to develop and keep current a catalog of applicable risks associated with the organization's business operations and technologies in use.

controls.title: Risk Assessment
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to conduct recurring assessments of risk that includes the likelihood and magnitude of harm, from unauthorized access, use, disclosure, disruption, modification or destruction of the organization's Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD).

controls.title: Risk Register
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to maintain a risk register that facilitates monitoring and reporting of risks.

controls.title: Risk Ranking
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to identify and assign a risk ranking to newly discovered security vulnerabilities that is based on industry-recognized practices.

controls.title: Risk Remediation
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to remediate risks to an acceptable level.

controls.title: Risk Response
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to ensure proper risk response actions were performed to remediate findings from security, compliance and/or resilience-related:
(1) Assessments;
(2) Audits; and/or
(3) Incidents.

controls.title: Compensating Countermeasures
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to identify and implement compensating countermeasures to reduce risk and exposure to threats.

controls.title: Risk Assessment Update
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to routinely update risk assessments and react accordingly upon identifying new security vulnerabilities, including using outside sources for security vulnerability information.

controls.title: Business Impact Analysis (BIA)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to conduct a Business Impact Analysis (BIA) to identify and assess security, compliance and resilience risks.

controls.title: Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM) Plan
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to develop a plan for Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM) associated with the development, acquisition, maintenance and disposal of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS), including documenting selected mitigating actions and monitoring performance against those plans.

controls.title: Supply Chain Risk Assessment
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to periodically assess supply chain risks associated with Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).

controls.title: Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to conduct a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) on Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) that store, process and/or transmit Personal Data (PD) to identify and remediate reasonably-expected risks.

controls.title: Risk Culture
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure teams are committed to a culture that considers and communicates technology-related risk.

controls.title: Security, Compliance & Resilience-Minded Workforce
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of security workforce development and awareness controls.

controls.title: Security, Compliance & Resilience Awareness Training
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to provide all employees and contractors appropriate security, compliance and resilience awareness education and training that is relevant for their job function.

controls.title: Social Engineering & Mining
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to include awareness training on recognizing and reporting potential and actual instances of social engineering and social mining.

controls.title: Role-Based Security, Compliance & Resilience Training
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to provide role-based security, compliance and resilience-related training: 
(1) Before authorizing access to the system or performing assigned duties; 
(2) When required by system changes; and 
(3) Annually thereafter.

controls.title: Suspicious Communications & Anomalous System Behavior
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to provide training to personnel on organization-defined indicators of malware to recognize suspicious communications and anomalous behavior.

controls.title: Sensitive / Regulated Data Storage, Handling & Processing
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure that every user accessing a system processing, storing or transmitting sensitive/regulated data is formally trained in data handling requirements.

controls.title: Privileged Users
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to provide specific training for privileged users to ensure privileged users understand their unique roles and responsibilities

controls.title: Cyber Threat Environment
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to provide role-based security, compliance and resilience awareness training that is current and relevant to the cyber threats that users might encounter in day-to-day business operations.

controls.title: Continuing Professional Education (CPE) - Security, Compliance & Resilience Personnel
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure security, compliance and resilience personnel receive Continuing Professional Education (CPE) training to maintain currency and proficiency with industry-recognized secure practices that are pertinent to their assigned roles and responsibilities.

controls.title: Continuing Professional Education (CPE) - DevOps Personnel
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure application development and operations (DevOps) personnel receive Continuing Professional Education (CPE) training on Secure Software Development Practices (SSDP) to appropriately address evolving threats.

controls.title: Security, Compliance & Resilience Training Records
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to document, retain and monitor individual training activities, including:
(1) Initial security, compliance and resilience awareness training;
(2) Recurring awareness training; and
(3) Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)-specific training.

controls.title: Secure Engineering Principles
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of industry-recognized security, compliance and resilience practices in the specification, design, development, implementation and modification of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).

controls.title: Centralized Management of Security, Compliance & Resilience Controls
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to centrally-manage the organization-wide management and implementation of security, compliance and resilience controls and related processes.

controls.title: Achieving Resilience Requirements
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to achieve resilience requirements in normal and adverse situations.

controls.title: Alignment With Enterprise Architecture
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to develop an enterprise architecture, aligned with industry-recognized leading practices, with consideration for security, compliance and resilience principles that addresses risk to organizational operations, assets, individuals and other organizations.

controls.title: Standardized Terminology
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to standardize technology and process terminology to reduce confusion amongst groups and departments.

controls.title: Technical Debt Reviews
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to conduct ongoing “technical debt” reviews of hardware and software technologies to remediate outdated and/or unsupported technologies.

controls.title: Defense-In-Depth (DiD) Architecture
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement security functions as a layered structure minimizing interactions between layers of the design and avoiding any dependence by lower layers on the functionality or correctness of higher layers.

controls.title: Security Function Isolation
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to isolate security functions from non-security functions.

controls.title: Predictable Failure Analysis
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to determine the Mean Time to Failure (MTTF) for system components in specific environments of operation.

controls.title: Technology Lifecycle Management
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to manage the usable lifecycles of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).

controls.title: Change Processing & Storage Locations
controls.description: Automated mechanisms exist to change the location of processing and/or storage at random time intervals.

controls.title: Secure Log-On Procedures
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize a trusted communications path between the user and the security functions of the system.

controls.title: Clock Synchronization
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize time-synchronization technology to synchronize all critical system clocks.

controls.title: Technology Development & Acquisition
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of tailored development and acquisition strategies, contract tools and procurement methods to meet unique business needs.

controls.title: Product Management
Integrity Mechanisms for Software / Firmware Updates
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize integrity validation mechanisms for security updates.

controls.title: Minimum Viable Product (MVP) Security Requirements
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to design, develop and produce Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) in such a way that risk-based technical and functional specifications ensure Minimum Viable Product (MVP) criteria establish an appropriate level of security and resiliency based on applicable risks and threats.

controls.title: Ports, Protocols & Services In Use
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to require the developers of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to identify early in the Secure Development Life Cycle (SDLC), the functions, ports, protocols and services intended for use.

controls.title: Development Methods, Techniques & Processes
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to require software developers to ensure that their software development processes employ industry-recognized secure practices for secure programming, engineering methods, quality control processes and validation techniques to minimize flawed and/or malformed software.

controls.title: Identification & Justification of Ports, Protocols & Services
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to require process owners to identify, document and justify the business need for the ports, protocols and other services necessary to operate their technology solutions.

controls.title: Insecure Ports, Protocols & Services
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to mitigate the risk associated with the use of insecure ports, protocols and services necessary to operate technology solutions.

controls.title: Documentation Requirements
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to obtain, protect and distribute administrator documentation for Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) that describe:
(1) Secure configuration, installation and operation of the TAAS;
(2) Effective use and maintenance of security features/functions; and
(3) Known vulnerabilities regarding configuration and use of administrative (e.g., privileged) functions.

controls.title: Software Bill of Materials (SBOM)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to generate, or obtain, a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) for Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) that lists software packages in use, including versions and applicable licenses.

controls.title: Developer Architecture & Design
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to require the developers of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to produce a design specification and security architecture that: 
(1) Is consistent with and supportive of the organization's security architecture which is established within and is an integrated part of the organization's enterprise architecture;
(2) Accurately and completely describes the required security functionality and the allocation of security, compliance and resilience controls among physical and logical components; and
(3) Expresses how individual security functions, mechanisms and services work together to provide required security capabilities and a unified approach to protection.

controls.title: Physical Diagnostic & Test Interfaces
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to secure physical diagnostic and test interfaces to prevent misuse.

controls.title: Secure Software Development Practices (SSDP)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to develop applications based on Secure Software Development Practices (SSDP).

controls.title: Criticality Analysis During Development
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to require the developer of the Technology Asset, Application and/or Service (TAAS) to perform a criticality analysis at organization-defined decision points in the Secure Development Life Cycle (SDLC).

controls.title: Threat Modeling
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to perform threat modelling and other secure design techniques, to ensure that threats to software and solutions are identified and accounted for.

controls.title: Software Assurance Maturity Model (SAMM)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize a Software Assurance Maturity Model (SAMM) to govern a secure development lifecycle for the development of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).

controls.title: Software Design Review
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to have an independent review of the software design to validate:
(1) Applicable security, compliance and resilience requirements are met; and
(2) Identified risks are remediated.

controls.title: Secure Development Environments
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to maintain a segmented development network to ensure a secure development environment.

controls.title: Separation of Development, Testing and Operational Environments
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to manage separate development, testing and operational environments to reduce the risks of unauthorized access or changes to the operational environment and to ensure no impact to production Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).

controls.title: Secure Migration Practices
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure secure migration practices purge Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) of test/development/staging data and accounts before it is migrated into a production environment.

controls.title: Security, Compliance & Resilience Testing Throughout Development
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to require system developers/integrators consult with security, compliance and/or resilience personnel to: 
(1) Create and implement a Security Testing and Evaluation (ST&E) plan, or similar capability;
(2) Implement a verifiable flaw remediation process to correct weaknesses and deficiencies identified during the control testing and evaluation process; and
(3) Document the results.

controls.title: Continuous Monitoring Plan
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to require the developers of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to produce a plan for the continuous monitoring of security, compliance and/or resilience control effectiveness.

controls.title: Static Code Analysis
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to require the developers of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to employ static code analysis tools to identify and remediate common flaws and document the results of the analysis.

controls.title: Dynamic Code Analysis
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to require the developers of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to employ dynamic code analysis tools to identify and remediate common flaws and document the results of the analysis.

controls.title: Malformed Input Testing
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize testing methods to ensure Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) continue to operate as intended when subject to invalid or unexpected inputs on its interfaces.

controls.title: Application Penetration Testing
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to perform application-level penetration testing of custom-made Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).

controls.title: Use of Live Data
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to approve, document and control the use of live data in development and test environments.

controls.title: Developer Screening
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure that the developers of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) have the requisite skillset and appropriate access authorizations.

controls.title: Developer Configuration Management
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to require system developers and integrators to perform configuration management during system design, development, implementation and operation.

controls.title: Software / Firmware Integrity Verification
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to require developers of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to enable integrity verification of software and firmware components.

controls.title: Hardware Integrity Verification
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to require developers of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to enable integrity verification of hardware components.

controls.title: Developer Threat Analysis & Flaw Remediation
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to require system developers and integrators to develop and implement an ongoing Security Testing and Evaluation (ST&E) plan, or similar process, to objectively identify and remediate vulnerabilities prior to release to production.

controls.title: Unsupported Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)
controls.description:
Mechanisms exist to prevent unsupported Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) by:
(1) Removing and/or replacing TAAS when support for the components is no longer available from the developer, vendor or manufacturer; and
(2) Requiring justification and documented approval for the continued use of unsupported TAAS required to satisfy mission/business needs.

controls.title: Input Data Validation
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to check the validity of information inputs.

controls.title: Access to Program Source Code
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to limit privileges to change software resident within software libraries.

controls.title: Threat Intelligence Program
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to implement a threat intelligence program that includes a cross-organization information-sharing capability that can influence the development of the system and security architectures, selection of security solutions, monitoring, threat hunting, response and recovery activities.

controls.title: Indicators of Exposure (IOE)
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to develop Indicators of Exposure (IOE) to understand the potential attack vectors that attackers could use to attack the organization.

controls.title: Threat Intelligence Feeds
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to maintain situational awareness of vulnerabilities and evolving threats by leveraging the knowledge of attacker tactics, techniques and procedures to facilitate the implementation of preventative and compensating controls.

controls.title: Threat Intelligence Reporting
controls.description: Mechanisms exist to utilize external threat intelligence feeds to generate and disseminate organization-specific security alerts, advisories and/or directives.

controls.title: Insider Threat Program
